Help

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Strive for Animal Welfare (SAW), and what do you do?

SAW is a community-driven animal welfare initiative working to improve how people understand, treat and relate to animals. We promote animal welfare through education, community engagement, protection and practical action.

What animal welfare issues does SAW focus on?

Our work covers companion, working and aquatic animals, delivered through our WAAGS school clubs, community education, and our working animal and aquatic animal welfare initiatives.

Does SAW provide animal rescue or emergency response?

SAW’s work centres on education, community engagement, protection and practical action. If you know of an animal in need, send us the details through our contact page and we will advise on the best next step.

How can my school or community participate in SAW’s education and advocacy programmes?

Get in touch through our contact page and tell us about your school or community. We will recommend the programme that fits best, such as WAAGS for schools or Community Animal Welfare Education for community groups.

How can I volunteer or support SAW?

Share your details on our contact page and let us know how you would like to help. We will reach out about volunteering, partnerships and other ways to support our work.
